speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing episodic cough and shortness of breath; to begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and do you have any history of asthma or respiratory conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pertussis (whooping cough). The clinical picture of a nonproductive cough worsening at night, a one-month duration, and a preceding viral prodrome of fever and congestion is highly characteristic. I am ready to proceed with diagnostic confirmation or treatment planning.
